quarterly_data.signal: Group CFO Genuino Christino: Q2 2026 EBITDA improved to $2.1 billion, a margin of $155 per ton, well above previous through-the-cycle averages; the European segment delivered EBITDA of $98 per ton, a three-year high, not yet reflecting the new TRQ trade tool.
quarterly_data.figure: EBITDA $2.1 billion; $155 per ton; Europe $98 per ton

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: third-quarter shipments guided stable to higher than Q2, a counter-seasonal outcome; IR head Daniel Fairclough: all steel segments are expected to improve sequentially in Q3 on higher shipments and higher average selling prices, partly offset by higher carbon costs, and positive free cash flow is reiterated for this year and beyond.

Europe (CFO): production restarts announced in Spain, Poland and more recently France; from August/Q3 the full suite of blast furnaces in Europe is in operation; order book is getting stronger, with bookings already for Q4, and prices are bucking normal seasonal trends; the restarted tons are expected to be more profitable through fixed-cost absorption, offset partly by higher carbon costs.
CFO: underlying free cash flow in the first half annualized at $2.5 billion, excluding seasonal working capital investment and strategic growth capex.

Strategic growth projects (CFO): expected to contribute new incremental EBITDA of $1.8 billion from 2026 onwards; $700 million of the $1.8 billion should be captured this year, $300 million already in H1 and another $400 million he believes should be captured in H2; Liberia, the Serra Azul expansion and the U.S. EAF are to be completed this year.
quarterly_data.figure: $1.8 billion incremental EBITDA; $300 million in H1; $400 million in H2

quarterly_data.signal: Growth options (CFO): long-term plan to grow India capacity to 40 million tons per annum; evaluating downstream growth in Brazil; advancing studies and engineering work for a potential second EAF at Calvert (IR head Daniel Fairclough: moving forward with the detailed engineering; it would make Calvert less dependent on imported sources of slab); Liberia offers further growth optionality.

Calvert, U.S. (IR head Daniel Fairclough): the first EAF continues to ramp up, with full capacity expected to be achieved later in this second half of the year; it can produce the most demanding exposed automotive grades; the new electrical steels project producing non-grain-oriented steels is progressing to plan.

Liberia mining (CFO): two concentrator lines running and the third getting ready to start; 18 million tons guidance maintained, requiring about 10 million tons shipped in H2; heavy rainy-season shipment delays expected to be caught up in Q3.
quarterly_data.figure: 18 million tons; about 10 million tons in H2

quarterly_data.signal: Brazil (CFO): facilities are running at full capacity with all furnaces running; the group can divert slabs (3 million tons of slabs plus Tubarao also producing slabs) to Europe if needed.

Sustainable solutions (CFO, answering a question on the division's EBITDA): run rate already in excess of $500 million; another gigawatt of renewable capacity is being developed in India; sustainable construction (panels, profiles) is expanding into India and the U.S., including a recently acquired company in Brazil and a U.S. greenfield.
quarterly_data.figure: run rate in excess of $500 million

quarterly_data.signal: India and JVs (CFO): record Q2 shipments at a run rate of about 8 million tonnes; capacity there is being doubled; demand strong and prices recovered; CFO: India steel demand expected to approximately double over the next decade.

Management view on demand: CFO - steel is a critical enabler of electrification, renewable energy and data center infrastructure; IR head Daniel Fairclough - almost 300 million tons of steel would be required for electrification goals through 2035, ex-China, using external assumptions (company slide 19).

Europe policy (IR head Daniel Fairclough): CBAM in place since January 1 and the new TRQ trade tool since 'the beginning of this month'; ETS review proposals are 'a step in the right direction'; he expects it is 'probably just a question of time before slabs become part of TRQ'. CFO: real demand in Europe is stable after prior declines; imports should be lower and ArcelorMittal expects to regain market share.

CFO on decarbonization: DRI in Europe is not part of current plans; ArcelorMittal operates the only DRI plant in Europe, in Hamburg; the focus is Dunkirk; investment only when it earns a decent return.
